question_defect: The stem gives the mass the symbol 'm' and then writes the loop radius as '2m' in the same sentence, so the radius reads literally as two times the mass; only the options, which are lengths in metres, settle that it means 2 metres.
notes: Solved blind first by a different route: 'just completes' the loop needs v_bottom = sqrt(5gR) = sqrt(5*10*2) = 10 m/s, so h = v^2/(2g) = 5 m. The solution's route (minimum speed at the top, then energy conservation to the top of the loop) reaches the same value; recomputed each line: v^2_top = gR = 20 m^2/s^2, mgh = mg(2R) + 0.5mv^2 gives h = 2R + R/2 = 2.5R = 5 m. All three common_mistakes routes recomputed and each lands on the option it names: cm[0] h read off as R = 2 m (option 1), cm[1] 2 m taken as the diameter so R = 1 m and 5R/2 = 5/2 m (option 2), cm[2] the rule misremembered as h = 5R giving 10 m (option 4). None of them condemns a correct method. Plain-language pass; difficulty 'medium' and mistake_type_hint 'application' both fit a two-stage energy-plus-circular-motion item.
